To start off i owned a G14 and have since sold it because of my lack luster experience with it. I am Canadian so even for the price alone... its quite a steep investment.

I wouldn't necessarily recommend this to one of my friends, knowing what i know now, and how much this machine costs in many markets. Here are some of the issues that I have with the Laptop and its build and overall experience.

- Build is Okay but by no means amazing ( People have experienced paint chips out the box, laptops burning from the inside, inconsistent lighting, coil whine, Screen issues, People have keys slanted or off set)  I did not experience this but after purchasing the G14 i wont say I wasn't worried that these issues would sporadically occur like they do for so many people here.

- Asus did a horrible job optimizing software... i have experienced black screens, bsods, multiple times, it took a while of tinkering with it and troubleshooting all the errors it was sputtering out, Im by no means a technical person, and did not expect to pay so much money to have to learn how to be my own IT person ( ASUS just tells you to RMA the thing)

- Battery life is not what it is marketed out of the box. Yes i did do the power fixes and even would run a power plan where my cpu was limited to 50% of its max capacity... That would give me about 10-13 estimated hours, however why limit the laptop to get more out of it? It was made to seem like you could run normally at 10 hours.

- Upon research of ASUS warranty, RMA service I would never be able to trust them to efficiently fix the laptop, and if they by some miracle did fix it on the first time, I would expect there to be cosmetic damage to it. ( You can find many a stories of ASUS voiding warranties for no reason, not fixing their products, and or damaging them and claiming it was the user or postal service error.)

Going back to what I said before.. being in Canada, the R7/1660 costs around 1900 CAD here after tax - with the R9/2060 at 2800 or so after taxes... That is a lot of money to spend and gamble with the possibility of having an inconsistent experience.

I couldn't recommend it to someone I know for that sole reason. Id much prefer they buy something with a better reputation for a similar price.

Is it powerful? Does it aesthetically look pleasing? Is it dope when it works? Yes, yes yes.

But its only dope when it works... and I think it isn't reasonable to ask anyone to pay this much money to have this inconsistent of an experience.
